messages:
mina: Anyone else seeing intermittent TLS failures for requests to eu-west inference endpoints? Started ~15:00 UTC, ~2% of requests get TLS handshake failures from ALB :eyes:
lorenzo: seeing the same in metrics, spikes of TLS_HANDSHAKE_ERROR in edge logs around 15:02. Mostly to /v1/generate on dedicated pools.
alex: I pulled the ALB access logs for that window — some lines show TLS alert when forwarding to targetgroup. snippet: 
```
  request_processing_time:0.000
  target_processing_time:0.004
  response_processing_time:0.001
  elb_status_code: 502
  target_status_code: 0
  ssl_cipher: ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
  ssl_protocol: TLSv1.2
  tls_alert: handshake_failure
```
sree: interesting — I also saw some clients report certificate mismatch when hitting the same host. curl -v shows the certificate being served is a *.redwood.prod wildcard, but that route should be serving service-specific cert (we upload cert per-route via ALB listener rules).
mina: here's an openssl s_client dump from one failing client (truncated):
```
$ openssl s_client -connect api-eu.redwood.prod:443 -servername service-a.eu.redwood.prod
CONNECTED(00000003)
1400...: SSL handshake has read 0 bytes and written 320 bytes
---
no peer certificate available
---
ssl handshake failure
```
lorenzo: hmm, 'no peer certificate available' — could be TLS being terminated earlier (proxy) and a TCP passthrough expected SNI but missing. Did anything change to the ALB listener or ingress annotations in the last deploy?
deploy-bot: deploy-17324 completed to infra/alb-config at 14:58 UTC — change: removed `ssl-protocols: TLSv1.3` override, rolled back later at 15:10.
alex: That deploy touched listener rules for the eu-west ALB — specifically switched the listener to use SNI-based cert selection with a default wildcard fallback. I suspect the SNI isn't making it through in some flow so default wildcard is returned which doesn't satisfy downstream mTLS expectations.
sree: Could the client traffic be coming via our NAT/egress path (mesh-egress) that rewrites SNI? There was a recent NAT gateway change in that AZ (ticket INF-847). If connections are coming from internal egress proxies, SNI might be stripped or rewritten.
mina: I repro locally by sending traffic via the egress proxy and I get the wildcard cert instead of the route cert. When I hit the ALB directly from my workstation with correct SNI header it's fine. So the path matters.
lorenzo: That aligns — path A: direct client -> ALB (SNI intact) -> correct cert. Path B: client -> egress-proxy/NAT -> ALB (clienthello modified or absent) -> ALB falls back to default cert.
alex: We should confirm whether the egress proxy is doing TLS termination or SNI rewriting. @sree can you check the proxy config (nginx/haproxy) for `proxy_ssl_server_name` or `ssl_preread` settings?
sree: on it. quick grep shows `ssl_preread` enabled for TCP passthrough but we have a new HAProxy sidecar (rolled on 14:55) that has `ssl_fc_sni` logic and a default-backend rewrite. Looks like the sidecar could be replacing SNI when routing to ALB.
mina: action: revert the sidecar change on the egress path to preserve client SNI. I'll open a rollback PR and patch the sidecar template.
alex: also add a short-term mitigation: add a fallback certificate with the correct SANs for the affected services to the ALB default cert set (so even if SNI missing, clients still see a valid cert).
lorenzo: +1. Also let's add logging to detect SNI-less clienthellos at the ALB level — can we enable TLS ClientHello logging for the problematic listener for a short window? That will help confirm.
sree: enabling extra logging now for 20m. will post findings.
mina: I'll coordinate the rollback. tagging infra-oncall to watch for regression: @infra-oncall please standby.
deploy-bot: rollback-17325 queued (target: infra/egress-sidecar) by mina at 15:34 UTC — estimated 3m to complete.
mina: rollback applied, mirroring requests now show correct certs in my quick check. Will monitor metrics for the next 30m. :thumbsup:
lorenzo: thanks. follow-ups: 1) add e2e test that exercises path via egress proxy, 2) harden sidecar config to never rewrite SNI for external endpoints, 3) add an alert for TLS default-cert usage rate > 0.5% of requests for a route.
mina: created INF-912 to track follow-ups and added owners. anyone wants to add anything else?
alex: can we also add a canary step when changing ALB listener behavior (SNI cert selection) — small % first.
sree: noted, will add to deployment runbook.
mina: closing thread for now, will update when the 30m window completes. thanks all.
